drhp.business: The Company is primarily engaged in the business of manufacturing and repairing of electrical equipment, mainly transformers, and there has been no change in the nature of the business during the year under review. It operates two manufacturing units - Bhubaneswar (Odisha) and Baroda (Gujarat) - and sells largely to state electricity distribution companies, having secured Rate Contracts with the TP-group Odisha discoms and a Letter of Award for 10 kVA distribution transformers at the Baroda unit. As at 31 March 2026 the Company had no subsidiaries, associates or joint ventures.

risks.note: MD&A Risks and Concerns states the industry is highly sensitive to these prices and that sudden increases raise production costs which may not be easily passed on to customers, thus impacting profit margins - acute for a rate-contract order book where prices are fixed in advance.
risks.risk: Raw material price volatility (copper, steel, insulation oil)

risks.note: MD&A flags that the industry operates on large projects with extended payment cycles, and that delays in payments from clients, particularly government entities or large corporations, can strain cash flow and the ability to meet operational expenses. The disclosed order book is concentrated in state distribution utility rate contracts (TPSODL, TPWODL, TPCODL).
risks.risk: Credit risk and extended payment cycles with utility customers

risks.note: The Board's Report states the Company requires working capital of Rs 15.00 crores to execute the existing orders at both units at 2,000-2,500 transformers per month, and recommends the Managing Director explore strategic investors or capital infusion for the Baroda Unit - order execution is therefore contingent on funding being arranged.
risks.risk: Working capital dependency for order execution

risks.note: MD&A notes the transformers market is highly competitive with numerous players vying for market share, and that intense competition can lead to price wars, squeezing profit margins and making profitability difficult to maintain.

MD&A states demand is closely tied to the economic health of the power, industrial and infrastructure sectors, and that economic slowdowns, reduced infrastructure investment or delays in government projects can lead to decreased demand and excess production capacity.
risks.risk: Demand fluctuation tied to government and infrastructure spending

risks.note: MD&A notes reliance on a global supply chain for raw materials and components, with geopolitical tensions, natural disasters or logistical issues causing production delays and increased costs.

MD&A states the pace of technological change is accelerating and companies that fail to keep up risk becoming obsolete, with adoption requiring substantial investment in R&D, training and equipment; it separately flags cybersecurity threats as smart-grid and IoT-enabled devices are adopted.
risks.risk: Technology obsolescence and the shift to smart transformers

risks.note: MD&A flags that unexpected changes in tariffs, import/export regulations and environmental standards create uncertainty and may require significant investment in technology upgrades, while stricter environmental rules on emissions, waste and eco-friendly materials raise production costs, with penalties, reputational damage and loss of market access for non-compliance.

sk.overview: Powerica operates across two industries: (1) India's standby power / diesel-generator (DG set) market, where DG sets, UPS, inverters and battery storage provide backup power during outages/voltage fluctuations across commercial, manufacturing, IT/data-centre, telecom and infrastructure sectors (F&S Report); and (2) India's wind power sector within the broader renewable energy industry, where wind plays a pivotal role in the country's energy transition (CRISIL Report).
